correctness.rationale: All geometry and quantifiers are explicit. For each fixed cut ratio, exact edge sine-correlation integration gives the first variation. The sine rule transforms the removed area into a one-variable coefficient. The smooth function is positive in the sector with correct parallel zeros, and a reflection comparison rules out half the angles. Its derivative numerator divided by theta^2 is strictly decreasing by a finite exact Taylor coefficient table and a uniform tenth-derivative remainder bound over every real theta in (0,pi/6); boundary signs force exactly one optimizer. The included checker verifies identities, rational bounds, and independent polygon projection integrations. Finite quadrature is only a numerical cross-check.

value.rationale: The first-public source deliberately highlights a counterintuitive perturbation contrast: parallel cuts worsen width dispersion but oblique cuts improve it. Fixed removed area is the natural cost constraint, so the unknown best orientation and its exact efficiency are motivated questions, not arbitrary coefficient extraction. The new sharp response, asymmetric ratio and uniqueness (with all-angle inequality) provide a meaningful structural and quantitative answer; the theorem does not purport to solve global quadrilateral width minimization.
